title: Best Tuna Melt for the Hall (Diner Style)
displayTitle: Best Tuna Melt for the Hall (Diner Style)
seoTitle: Best Tuna Melt for the Hall (Diner Style) | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Open-faced tuna melts on rye with cheddar — sheet-pan batch for the crew
subtitle: Open-faced tuna melts on rye with cheddar — sheet-pan batch for the crew
description: Well-drained tuna folds into a seasoned salad, spreads onto buttered rye, and tops with sharp cheddar for a sheet-pan broil until every melt bubbles. Open-faced means faster batch cooking and an obvious tuna-melt identity — no mystery hot sandwiches.

ingredients.name: canned tuna
ingredients.notes: in water, drained and pressed dry

steps.title: Drain tuna and make the salad
steps.instruction: Open tuna, drain, and press dry in a colander or on paper towels — dry tuna is the difference between melts and mush. Fold with mayonnaise, celery, onion, lemon, Dijon, salt, and pepper until creamy but not soupy. Taste and adjust acid.

steps.title: Butter rye and portion salad
steps.instruction: Heat broiler with rack in upper third. Butter one side of each rye slice and lay buttered-side down on parchment-lined sheet pans. Spread a generous ½ cup tuna salad on each slice, mounding slightly in the center.

steps.title: Top with cheddar
steps.instruction: Cover each open face with cheddar — sliced or grated — all the way to the edges so broiler melt seals to bread. Dust lightly with paprika if you want diner color.

steps.title: Broil until bubbling
steps.instruction: Broil until cheese melts, bubbles, and browns in spots, 4–6 minutes — rotate pans and watch constantly. Cheese should look glossy and split at the edges, not pale and rubbery. Target oven/smoker temperature: 500°F.

steps.title: Hold warm and serve open-faced
steps.instruction: Slide melts onto serving platters or leave on parchment in a 200°F oven up to 15 minutes. Serve open-faced with pickles so the crew sees tuna and rye immediately. Re-broil 1 minute if cheese tightens on hold.

proTips: A squeeze of hot sauce in the salad wakes up canned tuna without hiding it.
For 14, use two ovens or stagger pans — crowded broilers steam instead of brown.
Do not cover finished melts with foil — condensation kills crisp rye.
tonightSpread: Open-faced tuna melts with pickle chips and tomato soup on the side if available.
Simple potato chips or slaw — this sandwich is the main event.
leftovers: Tuna salad keeps 2 days refrigerated — broil fresh bread tomorrow.
Fold leftover salad into a pasta bake with extra cheddar.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Tuna melts are cheap, fast, and familiar — perfect when the crew wants comfort without firing up the smoker. Sheet-pan broiling beats one-at-a-time skillets when ten people walk in together after a call.
mealPrepNotes: Mix tuna salad up to 6 hours ahead; cover and refrigerate. Butter rye and portion salad onto trays just before broiling so bread does not sog. Hold finished melts in a warm oven 200°F up to 15 minutes — cheese sets but reheats fine under broiler 1 minute.
